faqs.question: What is IMA™?
faqs.answer: IMA™ is a hyperspectral microscope from Photon etc. that captures spatial and spectral information across the 400–1620 nm range.

faqs.question: What is IMA™ used for?
faqs.answer: IMA™ is used for hyperspectral characterization of advanced materials, solar cells, nanomaterials, semiconductors, infrared markers, transparent materials, crystals, polymers and other research samples.

faqs.question: What wavelength range does IMA™ cover?
faqs.answer: IMA™ provides hyperspectral coverage from 400 to 1620 nm, spanning the VIS, NIR and SWIR regions.

faqs.question: What does IMA™ measure?
faqs.answer: IMA™ can rapidly map photoluminescence, electroluminescence, fluorescence, reflectance and transmittance.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ measure photoluminescence?
faqs.answer: Yes. IMA™ supports photoluminescence mapping and Photon etc. demonstrates the system for PL mapping of perovskite crystals.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ measure electroluminescence?
faqs.answer: Yes. IMA™ can map electroluminescence and is positioned for applications including solar-cell and semiconductor research.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ perform fluorescence imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. IMA™ supports hyperspectral fluorescence imaging.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ measure reflectance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reflectance is one of the measurement modes supported by IMA™.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ measure transmittance?
faqs.answer: Yes. IMA™ supports transmittance measurements for suitable samples.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ be configured as a darkfield microscope?
faqs.answer: Yes. IMA™ can be configured as either a brightfield or darkfield hyperspectral microscope.

faqs.question: What samples can be studied using darkfield IMA™?
faqs.answer: Photon etc. identifies transparent materials such as polymers, crystals and living cells as applications for hyperspectral darkfield microscopy.

faqs.question: How many data points can IMA™ acquire?
faqs.answer: Photon etc. states that IMA™ can acquire millions of data points in a single snapshot.

faqs.question: How is IMA™ different from point-by-point hyperspectral scanning?
faqs.answer: IMA™ uses high-throughput imaging filters for rapid hyperspectral acquisition, rather than relying on standard point-by-point scanning.

faqs.question: What type of microscope does IMA™ use?
faqs.answer: IMA™ combines a scientific-grade VIS, NIR and/or SWIR microscope with Photon etc.'s patented imaging filter technology.

faqs.question: Is IMA™ suitable for solar-cell research?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photon etc. identifies solar-cell research as an application and highlights PL and EL hyperspectral analysis.

faqs.question: Is IMA™ suitable for nanomaterial research?
faqs.answer: Yes. Advanced materials and nanomaterial analysis are listed among IMA™ applications.

faqs.question: Is IMA™ suitable for semiconductor analysis?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photon etc. identifies semiconductor quality control using hyperspectral PL and EL as an IMA™ application.

faqs.question: Can IMA™ be used for infrared marker research?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photon etc. identifies research involving infrared markers in complex environments, including tissues and living cells, using hyperspectral SWIR microscopy.

faqs.question: What is the price of IMA™ in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the required optical configuration, spectral range and application requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of IMA™ in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Photon etc. IMA™ in India.

longForm.heroLead: Capture spatial and spectral information from your sample in a single hyperspectral microscope. Photon etc. IMA™ is a hyperspectral microscope designed to acquire spatial and spectral information across the 400–1620 nm range. By combining a scientific-grade VIS, NIR and/or SWIR microscope with Photon etc.'s patented imaging filter technology, IMA™ enables detailed spectral characterization of a wide range of materials. IMA™ can acquire millions of data points in a single snapshot and rapidly map photoluminescence (PL), electroluminescence (EL), fluorescence, reflectance and transmittance. The system can be configured as either a brightfield or darkfield hyperspectral microscope, making it suitable for different sample types and imaging requirements. Unlike point-by-point scanning approaches, IMA™ uses high-throughput imaging filters to acquire hyperspectral information rapidly across the sample. IMA™ is suited to applications including advanced materials analysis, solar cell and nanomaterial research, semiconductor quality control, infrared marker studies, and hyperspectral imaging of transparent materials.

sections.title: How IMA™ Works
body: From a microscopic image to a hyperspectral data set
Traditional microscopy provides detailed spatial information about a sample. Hyperspectral microscopy adds spectral information to those spatial features.
IMA™ combines the two.
Sample → Microscopic imaging → Hyperspectral acquisition → Spatial + spectral data → Material characterization
Each measured region can therefore be considered in terms of both:
Where is the feature?
This is particularly useful when visually similar regions need to be distinguished by their optical or spectral properties.

faqs.question: What is the Photon etc. LIMA?
faqs.answer: The LIMA is a darkfield hyperspectral imaging microscope based on a tunable supercontinuum source. It illuminates the full field of view with continuously tunable, monochromatic, high power density laser light.

faqs.question: What excitation ranges are available on the LIMA?
faqs.answer: Four configurations: 400 to 1000 nm, 900 to 1620 nm, 1000 to 2500 nm and 400 to 1620 nm.

faqs.question: What is the spectral resolution of the LIMA?
faqs.answer: Excitation spectral resolution (FWHM) is 1.5 to 2.5 nm (400 to 1000 nm), 3.0 to 5.0 nm (900 to 1620 nm), < 5.0 nm (1000 to 2500 nm) and 1.5 to 5.0 nm (400 to 1620 nm).

faqs.question: What spatial resolution does the LIMA give?
faqs.answer: Spatial resolution is sub-micron, limited by the microscope objective NA, and near-diffraction-limited.

faqs.question: Can the LIMA image nanoparticles?
faqs.answer: Yes. Narrow-band illumination reduces phototoxicity and sample heating, and LIMA can image nanoparticles of several nm in size.

faqs.question: Which imaging modes does the LIMA support?
faqs.answer: Darkfield (oil and dry), brightfield, dia or epi illumination, and standard reflectance and transmittance imaging. It is also suited to photoluminescence excitation (PLE).

faqs.question: Which cameras are used with the LIMA?
faqs.answer: sCMOS (optionally CCD or EMCCD), ZephIR™ 1.7 or Alizé™ 1.7 InGaAs, and ZephIR™ 2.5 HgCdTe, depending on the configuration.

faqs.question: How is the LIMA faster than scanning systems?
faqs.answer: It maps the full spectral response of the field of view faster than point-by-point or line-scan systems.

faqs.question: What is the Photon etc. RIMA?
faqs.answer: The RIMA is a global hyperspectral Raman microscope. It delivers spectral and spatial information and rapidly provides Raman maps over large, megapixel-scale fields of view.

faqs.question: How is the RIMA different from point-by-point Raman mapping?
faqs.answer: RIMA uses high-throughput global-imaging filters, so a few monochromatic images build the hyperspectral data cube. Raster-scan methods must acquire a spectrum at every point or line, so RIMA is faster and more efficient.

faqs.question: Which excitation wavelengths are available on the RIMA?
faqs.answer: RIMA is available with 532 nm or 660 nm excitation (version 1) or 785 nm excitation (version 2).

faqs.question: What is the spectral range of the RIMA?
faqs.answer: 190 to 4000 cm⁻¹ with 532 or 660 nm excitation, and 190 to 2700 cm⁻¹ with 785 nm excitation. An anti-Stokes spectral range extension is available as an option.

faqs.question: What is the spectral and spatial resolution of the RIMA?
faqs.answer: Spectral resolution is below 7 cm⁻¹ (FWHM) and spatial resolution is sub-micron, limited by the microscope objective NA.

faqs.question: How fast does the RIMA acquire data?
faqs.answer: The maximum scanning speed is 150 ms per wavenumber.

faqs.question: Which objectives are available for the RIMA?
faqs.answer: 20X, 40X, 50X, 60X and 100X objectives are available as options.

faqs.question: What software does the RIMA use?
faqs.answer: PHySpec™ control and analysis software on a Windows 10, 64-bit PC, which is included.

faqs.question: What is the price of the RIMA™ in India?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the configuration and options. Contact Inkarp for a quotation on +91 8125580808 or info@inkarp.co.in.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor for the RIMA in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Photon etc. RIMA in India, with support for installation, training, AMC and application support.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.glanceDescription: Everything you need to evaluate the RIMA, including excitation versions, spectral range, imaging speed, stages, software and applications.
intro: The overview of the RIMA covers its role in global hyperspectral Raman imaging.

The Photon etc. RIMA is a hyperspectral microscope that combines spectral and spatial data. Global imaging needs only a few monochromatic images to build a hyperspectral data cube, while raster-scan methods must acquire a spectrum at every point or line in the field of view.
RIMA is available with 532 nm or 660 nm excitation (190 to 4000 cm⁻¹) or 785 nm excitation (190 to 2700 cm⁻¹), on an upright or inverted microscope, with PHySpec™ control and analysis software.

sections.title: The global hyperspectral Raman imaging workflow
sections.description: How the RIMA works, in a continuous loop of place, locate, excite, acquire and analyze.

steps.title: Place Sample
steps.description: The sample is placed on the stage: manual stage with 76 mm × 52 mm travel, or the optional motorized stage.

steps.title: Locate
steps.description: The region of interest is found with the megapixel video-mode camera and the selected objective.

steps.title: Excite
steps.description: The sample is excited at 532, 660 or 785 nm, depending on the version.

steps.title: Acquire
steps.description: Global imaging records monochromatic images across the continuously tunable spectral channels to build a hyperspectral data cube, at up to 150 ms per wavenumber.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.description: PHySpec™ applies preprocessing and spectrum extraction, with data saved in HDF5 or FITS.

sections.disclaimer: This workflow explanation is illustrative. Actual steps and settings depend on your sample, method and configuration.
